description:
The `npm-ci` gate is the Node-side CI gate carried by mcp-server issues, but its checker runs only the web workspace. A change confined to `mcp-server/` can pass every gate on its issue while the mcp-server test suite is failing.

## Background

`.jit/gates.toml` defines the `npm-ci` checker as `cd web && npm test -- --run && npm run lint && npm run build`. Its description calls it the "Web workspace checks" and the "web-side equivalent of cargo-ci". Nothing in it enters `mcp-server/`.

Issue a4e8d5ac (Align MCP system prompt with DAG-authoritative containment) carries `npm-ci` + `code-review` as its only gates and touches `mcp-server/index.js` exclusively. Its gates are therefore blind to `cd mcp-server && npm test`, whose integration suite fails at the time of filing (tool-count drift, tracked by c291e95c). The gate reported nothing.

`cargo-ci` covers the whole Rust workspace. The Node side has no equivalent covering both Node workspaces, so mcp-server has no automated gate at all.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-1: Every workspace with a test suite is reachable by some gate, and the gate carried by an issue that changes `mcp-server/` runs the mcp-server suite.
- [hard] REQ-2: Gate keys and descriptions state the workspaces each gate covers, so a gate cannot be selected for a workspace it does not exercise.
- [hard] REQ-3: The `mcp-server` suite passing is a precondition for an mcp-server-touching issue to reach Done, enforced by gate configuration rather than by convention.

## Notes

Consider whether `npm-ci` grows to span both Node workspaces or whether a distinct `mcp-ci` gate is registered alongside it. Changing an existing gate retroactively re-evaluates issues outside the filing epic; a new gate key does not. Discovered while executing epic dbe1e821; the gate hole is orthogonal to that epic and lives here.
title: Gate npm-ci does not cover the mcp-server test suite
